values.of: arguments and results of calls, messages of exceptions
values.types: None, bool, int, float, str, and list, tuple, set, frozenset, dict of those (two levels, the first items); other types keep their shape only
values.masked: values named like a secret (token, key, password, secret, auth, ...), the user and password of a URL, name=value pairs with such a name, long random strings; written as ***

not_collected.what: values of other types, and what is past the size limit
not_collected.reason: this recording was made with --values: the arguments and results of calls and the messages of exceptions are recorded when they are None, bool, int, float, str or a list, tuple, set or dict of those, cut at a size limit, with likely secrets written as ***. An object of another type has its shape only (writing it would run code of the program). Environment values, SQL parameters, file contents, request bodies and the arguments of logging records are not recorded

not_collected.what: calls outside user code
not_collected.reason: the standard library and installed packages are not recorded

not_collected.what: code compiled from a string under another name
not_collected.reason: code made with `compile` or `exec` is the program's when its file name is `<string>`, `<stdin>` or a notebook cell; under any other made-up name it is not recorded

not_collected.what: code of the program that runs in the middle of the recorder
not_collected.reason: a signal handler, a `__del__` or a weak reference callback that Python runs while Ormaos is noting an event is not recorded (Python reports no events then)

not_collected.what: exceptions that never pass through user code
not_collected.reason: only exceptions seen in a user-code frame are recorded

not_collected.what: which `except*` clause matched
not_collected.reason: for `except*` the handler line is the first clause of the `try`; several clauses can each take a part of the group, and which ones did is not recorded (the place is listed when it happens)

not_collected.what: io: contents
not_collected.reason: by design: no SQL parameters or literals, no file contents, no request or response bodies, no headers, no URL query strings

not_collected.what: io: results
not_collected.reason: rows returned or changed, bytes read or written and the exit status of a subprocess are not recorded

not_collected.what: io: reads and writes of a file that are not a method call
not_collected.reason: a read or a write is seen when Python code calls `read` or `write` on the file; iterating a file (`for line in f`, `csv.reader`) or `print(..., file=f)` happens inside C code, and only the `open` is seen (the files opened and never seen read or written are listed when it happens)

not_collected.what: io: sqlite3 statements, after the program sets a trace callback
not_collected.reason: sqlite3 has no event for statements, so Ormaos sets the trace callback of each connection. A callback the program had already set is kept and still called. When the program sets or clears the callback later, its choice stays and the statements after that are not recorded: this is reported for the connection when the call is made by Python code, and not when it is made from inside C code (`operator.methodcaller`, an extension module)

not_collected.what: io: other kinds
not_collected.reason: only sqlite3, files (`open`, `read`, `write`), subprocesses and HTTP through http.client (urllib, requests, urllib3) or httpx are recorded; not sockets, directory operations or `os.read` (listed with the line when they happen), and not other databases or anything a C library does by itself (never seen)

not_collected.what: io: the outcome of an `open` made from inside C code
not_collected.reason: an `open` is recorded when it is asked for; when it fails it is marked `raised` if Python code called it, and not otherwise

not_collected.what: io with no line of user code
not_collected.reason: I/O that no frame of user code is waiting for is not recorded: the import system and interpreter start (never counted), library threads and interpreter exit (counted when it happens)

not_collected.what: logs: the arguments and the formatted message
not_collected.reason: by design: of a logging record, the level, the logger, the line of your code and the message template are recorded, and how many arguments it had. A message that is not a string written in the code of the caller (an f-string, a text put together at run time) is a value: only its type and length are recorded

not_collected.what: logs: what happened to a record after the logger let it through
not_collected.reason: `dropped` means the level of the logger (or `logging.disable`) stopped the record before it was made. Whether a filter or the level of a handler stopped it later, and where it was written, is not recorded

not_collected.what: logs: records that do not go through `logging`
not_collected.reason: only the standard `logging` module is seen: not `print`, not `warnings`, not another logging library unless it hands its records to `logging`; a record with no line of your code waiting for it (a library thread) is counted, not recorded; what a library logs while it is being imported is not recorded

not_collected.what: dataframes: the cells
not_collected.reason: by design: of a pandas DataFrame or Series that a call receives or returns, only the number of rows and columns, the names and dtypes of the columns and the nulls per column are recorded. A column label that is text is recorded as a name (in a frame whose labels come from the data, a pivot, those labels are in the recording); a label that is not text is recorded by its type

not_collected.what: dataframes: frames that are not an argument or a result
not_collected.reason: a frame is described where a call of your code receives or returns it; not a frame inside a list or a dict, not a local variable, not a subclass of DataFrame or Series, and nothing when the program did not import pandas

not_collected.what: tensors: the numbers
not_collected.reason: by design: of a numpy array or a torch tensor that a call receives or returns, only the shape, the dtype, the device and the numeric health are recorded: how many NaN, how many inf, the smallest and the largest number (those two are numbers of the data)

not_collected.what: tensors: numeric health of some arrays
not_collected.reason: health is computed for float and integer dtypes, on the CPU, up to a size limit (listed when one is over it); not for bool, complex, object or text dtypes, sparse or quantized tensors, subclasses, arrays inside a list or a dict, and nothing when the program imported neither numpy nor torch

not_collected.what: path
not_collected.reason: line-by-line recording is off; ask for a scope with `ormaos run --path <file.py:function>`
